khee01.title: Day 1: “I'm fine”
khee01.caption:
Day 1 doesn't need a brave face. Feeling it means it mattered, and asking someone to come sit on the floor with you counts as progress.
Fine can wait.

khee02.title: The hoodie
khee02.caption: Still sleeping in their hoodie? You don't have to throw it out. Fold it, box it, put it on a shelf, and wrap yourself in something that's yours.

khee03.title: Rereading the whole chat
khee03.caption: The answer isn't hiding in old messages. Archive the chat and start a new note instead: a list of things you like about you. Save this for the night you want to scroll back.

khee04.title: Dinner for two, by habit
khee04.caption: Set out two plates without thinking? That care didn't leave with them. Feed yourself first, then text a friend to come eat the extra.

khee05.title: The “thriving” selfie
khee05.caption: You don't owe anyone proof that you're okay. Put the phone down, call someone real, and heal where nobody's watching.

khee06.title: The breakup spreadsheet
khee06.caption: Trying to solve the breakup like a puzzle you failed? Some answers never come, and you can still move forward. Close the laptop, take the walk, start a list of things you like.

khee07.title: “Was it my fault?”
khee07.caption: Polled every friend and still don't feel better? Friends can comfort you, but they can't decide for you. Ask yourself what you need right now, and write it down.

khee08.title: The 2 a.m. check
khee08.caption: Checking their page at 2 a.m. keeps the ache open. Muting them isn't a punishment, it's rest. Charge the phone across the room and let yourself sleep.

khee09.title: The escape trip
khee09.caption: Booked a flight to outrun the feelings? They pack themselves. Tonight, walk the block with a friend, and plan the trip later for joy.

khee10.title: Working through it
khee10.caption: Fourteen-hour days can feel like coping, but busy isn't the same as better. Log off, give the feelings ten minutes, and let rest count as healing.

khee11.title: “We're still friends!”
khee11.caption: Trying to be friends with your ex on day one? Space first isn't cold, it's kind. A friendship can come later, once it doesn't hurt.

khee12.title: Crying at everything
khee12.caption: Cried at a drawing of a dog? Tears are your heart doing the work. Drink some water, eat something, sleep. Send this to your friend who's crying at everything this week.

khee13.title: The emergency floor visit
khee13.caption: You don't need a speech when you're hurting, you need company. Let your friends in, even if the kitchen is a mess and you're lying on the floor.

khee14.title: The bad day on day 23
khee14.caption: One song and it feels like day one again. A bad day isn't starting over: healing goes up and down, and every day you've done still counts.

khee15.title: The first good morning
khee15.caption: The first morning they aren't your first thought feels strange, then quiet, then good. Healing isn't a parade. Notice it, and make a plan.
